cases.sentence: На бале должен был быть ___ и государь.
cases.explain: «дипломатический корпус» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: On the thirty-first of December, New Year’s Eve, 1809–10 an old grandee of Catherine’s day was giving a ball and midnight supper. The diplomatic corps and the Emperor himself were to be present.

cases.sentence: У освещенного подъезда с ___ стояла полиция, и не одни жандармы, но и полицеймейстер на подъезде и десятки офицеров полиции.
cases.explain: «красным сукном» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: The grandee’s well-known mansion on the English Quay glittered with innumerable lights. Police were stationed at the brightly lit entrance which was carpeted with red baize, and not only gendarmes but dozens of police officers and even the police master himself stood at the porch. Carriages kept driving away and fresh ones arriving, with red-liveried footmen and footmen in plumed hats. From the carriages emerged men wearing uniforms, stars, and ribbons, while ladies in satin and ermine cautiously descended the carriage steps which were let down for them with a clatter, and then walked hurriedly and noiselessly over the baize at the entrance.

cases.sentence: Экипажи отъезжали, и всё подъезжали новые с ___ и с лакеями в перьях на шляпах.
cases.explain: «красными лакеями» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: The grandee’s well-known mansion on the English Quay glittered with innumerable lights. Police were stationed at the brightly lit entrance which was carpeted with red baize, and not only gendarmes but dozens of police officers and even the police master himself stood at the porch. Carriages kept driving away and fresh ones arriving, with red-liveried footmen and footmen in plumed hats. From the carriages emerged men wearing uniforms, stars, and ribbons, while ladies in satin and ermine cautiously descended the carriage steps which were let down for them with a clatter, and then walked hurriedly and noiselessly over the baize at the entrance.

cases.sentence: Почти всякий раз, как подъезжал ___, в толпе пробегал шопот и снимались шапки.
cases.explain: «новый экипаж» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Almost every time a new carriage drove up a whisper ran through the crowd and caps were doffed.

cases.sentence: Вместе с Ростовыми ехала на бал Марья Игнатьевна Перонская, приятельница и родственница графини, худая и желтая фрейлина ___, руководящая провинциальных Ростовых в высшем петербургском свете.
cases.explain: «старого двора» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Márya Ignátevna Perónskaya, a thin and shallow maid of honor at the court of the Dowager Empress, who was a friend and relation of the countess and piloted the provincial Rostóvs in Petersburg high society, was to accompany them to the ball.

cases.sentence: Вместе с Ростовыми ехала на бал Марья Игнатьевна Перонская, приятельница и родственница графини, худая и желтая фрейлина старого двора, руководящая провинциальных Ростовых в высшем ___.
cases.explain: «петербургском свете» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Márya Ignátevna Perónskaya, a thin and shallow maid of honor at the court of the Dowager Empress, who was a friend and relation of the countess and piloted the provincial Rostóvs in Petersburg high society, was to accompany them to the ball.

cases.sentence: В 10 часов вечера Ростовы должны были заехать за фрейлиной к ___; а между тем было уже без пяти минут десять, а еще барышни не были одеты.
cases.explain: «Таврическому саду» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: They were to call for her at her house in the Taurida Gardens at ten o’clock, but it was already five minutes to ten, and the girls were not yet dressed.

cases.sentence: Все силы ее, с ___, были устремлены на то, чтоб они все: она, мама, Соня были одеты как нельзя лучше.
cases.explain: «самого утра» — after the preposition «с», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Natásha was going to her first grand ball. She had got up at eight that morning and had been in a fever of excitement and activity all day. All her powers since morning had been concentrated on ensuring that they all—she herself, Mamma, and Sónya—should be as well dressed as possible. Sónya and her mother put themselves entirely in her hands. The countess was to wear a claret-colored velvet dress, and the two girls white gauze over pink silk slips, with roses on their bodices and their hair dressed à la grecque.

cases.sentence: На графине должно было быть масака́ ___, на них двух белые дымковые платья на розовых, шелковых чехлах с розанами в корсаже.
cases.explain: «бархатное платье» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Natásha was going to her first grand ball. She had got up at eight that morning and had been in a fever of excitement and activity all day. All her powers since morning had been concentrated on ensuring that they all—she herself, Mamma, and Sónya—should be as well dressed as possible. Sónya and her mother put themselves entirely in her hands. The countess was to wear a claret-colored velvet dress, and the two girls white gauze over pink silk slips, with roses on their bodices and their hair dressed à la grecque.

cases.sentence: Соня, уже одетая, стояла посреди комнаты и, нажимая до боли ___, прикалывала последнюю визжавшую под булавкой ленту.
cases.explain: «маленьким пальцем» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Everything essential had already been done; feet, hands, necks, and ears washed, perfumed, and powdered, as befits a ball; the openwork silk stockings and white satin shoes with ribbons were already on; the hairdressing was almost done. Sónya was finishing dressing and so was the countess, but Natásha, who had bustled about helping them all, was behindhand. She was still sitting before a looking-glass with a dressing jacket thrown over her slender shoulders. Sónya stood ready dressed in the middle of the room and, pressing the head of a pin till it hurt her dainty finger, was fixing on a last ribbon that squeaked as the pin went through it.

cases.sentence: На бале решено было быть в половине одиннадцатого, а надо было еще Наташе одеться и заехать к ___.
cases.explain: «Таврическому саду» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: They had decided to be at the ball by half-past ten, and Natásha had still to get dressed and they had to call at the Taurida Gardens.

cases.sentence: Окончив прическу, Наташа в коротенькой юбке, из-под которой виднелись ___, и в материнской кофточке, подбежала к Соне, осмотрела ее и потом побежала к матери.
cases.explain: «бальные башмачки» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: When her hair was done, Natásha, in her short petticoat from under which her dancing shoes showed, and in her mother’s dressing jacket, ran up to Sónya, scrutinized her, and then ran to her mother. Turning her mother’s head this way and that, she fastened on the cap and, hurriedly kissing her gray hair, ran back to the maids who were turning up the hem of her skirt.

cases.sentence: Поворачивая ей голову, она приколола току, и, едва успев поцеловать ее ___, опять побежала к девушкам, подшивавшим ей юбку.
cases.explain: «седые волосы» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: When her hair was done, Natásha, in her short petticoat from under which her dancing shoes showed, and in her mother’s dressing jacket, ran up to Sónya, scrutinized her, and then ran to her mother. Turning her mother’s head this way and that, she fastened on the cap and, hurriedly kissing her gray hair, ran back to the maids who were turning up the hem of her skirt.

cases.sentence: Дело стояло за ___, которая была слишком длинна; ее подшивали две девушки, обкусывая торопливо нитки.
cases.explain: «наташиной юбкой» — after the preposition «за», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: The cause of the delay was Natásha’s skirt, which was too long. Two maids were turning up the hem and hurriedly biting off the ends of thread. A third with pins in her mouth was running about between the countess and Sónya, and a fourth held the whole of the gossamer garment up high on one uplifted hand.

cases.sentence: Он был в ___, чулках и башмаках, надушенный и припомаженный.
cases.explain: «синем фраке» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “In a minute! In a minute! Don’t come in, Papa!” she cried to her father as he opened the door—speaking from under the filmy skirt which still covered her whole face. Sónya slammed the door to. A minute later they let the count in. He was wearing a blue swallowtail coat, shoes and stockings, and was perfumed and his hair pomaded.

cases.sentence: В это время застенчиво, ___, вошла графиня в своей токе и бархатном платье.
cases.explain: «тихими шагами» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: At that moment, with soft steps, the countess came in shyly, in her cap and velvet gown.

cases.sentence: Но еще нужно было заехать к ___.
cases.explain: «Таврическому саду» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: At a quarter past ten they at last got into their carriages and started. But they had still to call at the Taurida Gardens.
